summary: The note examines the growing movement to bring nature-based learning into school curricula and compares outdoor learning with traditional indoor classrooms. Teacher, student and expert quotes plus several studies point to gains in engagement, academic performance, and social-emotional growth. It also covers obstacles such as weather, safety, and educator training, and notes professional development efforts, concluding that blending indoor and outdoor learning may work best.
one_line: Nature-based learning is gaining ground in schools, with studies showing engagement, academic and social-emotional benefits over traditional classrooms, despite logistical and training challenges.
key_facts: Since September 1, 2023, schools have increasingly moved learning outside the four-walled classroom.
Amanda Johnson of Greenfield Elementary School in Colorado reported on October 5, 2023 a marked improvement in her students' attentiveness and well-being after introducing outdoor lessons.
A study by the Environmental Education Research Foundation (EERF), dated November 12, 2023, found students in outdoor settings show increased engagement.
Jessica Li, a student at Riverbank High School in Oregon, said on December 1, 2023 that seeing and touching plants and animals makes lessons unforgettable.
A national survey in early 2024 pointed to a growing disconnection between traditional curriculum content and students' interests.
Dr. Henry Marsh, an educational psychologist, said on January 15, 2024 that many students feel they are simply being fed information without understanding its relevance.

A study in the Innovative Education Journal on February 20, 2024 found regular outdoor learning linked to improved problem-solving, better concentration, higher creativity, and increased overall academic performance.
Time outdoors has been linked to improved mental health and lower stress in students.
A Global Initiative for Children's Environmental Education (GICEE) project published on March 10, 2024 found outdoor education raises empathy toward peers and the environment.
Michael Thompson of Seaside Middle School in Florida said on April 3, 2024 that outside, students are 'more like friends working together'.
Challenges of outdoor education include weather, safety, access to natural spaces, and educators lacking training or resources.
The National Association for Environmental Education (NAEE) offers workshops and resources to help educators teach outdoors.
